correctness.rationale: Distributivity in the semiring of numerical-semigroup ideals gives all products of three generator types as additive generators H_(m,k), including mixed monomials; these are not Minkowski sums. For each of 14 relevant (m,k) cases, a membership recurrence is proved by strong induction. A verified absent Frobenius f followed by a full block of m^k consecutive present integers proves every larger integer present by closure; checking each remaining gap against every additive generator is an exhaustive PF criterion. A second independently written residue-Dijkstra reconstruction from actual certificates.json confirmed all 14 complete Apery representatives, genus, F and PF sets; m=8 cube PF {4023,4095,5223,5431,5503,5567,5791}. Cases m=2,3,4,5,6,7 exclude every smaller delayed failure, proving least m=8. Type 1 criterion for symmetry was applied with positive genus and exact F. This is finite exhaustion after a mathematically certified conductor, not unbounded extrapolation.

value.rationale: A delayed symmetry failure is a natural structural counterexample to persistence suggested by semiring ideal powers: a symmetric initial semigroup and symmetric square can nevertheless have type seven at the cube. The smallest parameter in consecutive triple generators, complete PF witness and Frobenius/genus profiles sharpen the immediate-square counterexamples in the motivating paper; no infinite classification is required for this boundary to be useful.
